meta.title: On-Device AI for Apple Silicon: uzu & Models | Mirai Labs
meta.description: Mirai Labs builds uzu, a Rust LLM engine for iPhone, iPad and Mac, and 4-bit/8-bit Qwen, LFM and Muse-Glimmer models benchmarked vs MLX and llama.cpp.

content.headline: Models, runtime & infrastructure to make on-device AI interactive, ambient & continuous.
content.subhead: The coming wave of AI products will be shaped by continuous interaction rather than one-off prompts and chat turns. That shift only works once latency stops being felt.

content.heading: The next decade collapses the app grid into one interface.
content.body: A single instruction, several services, no launches. The assistant settles the whole thing in one interaction instead of a dozen app switches.

content.heading: 1,000 t/s requires a different execution stack.
content.body: Interactive AI is never a single response. It is a loop that keeps running — parse, validate, rank, render — and every leg of it carries its own latency budget.

content.heading: On-device is not a smaller cloud.
content.body: It's a different system entirely — why can't we just run a cloud model on a device?

content.heading: Performance emerges from co-design across the stack.
content.body: On a phone or a laptop every request is handled on its own — nothing to batch it with and nowhere to parallelise. Mirai designs the model and the runtime together around that constraint.

content.heading: The full on-device stack to achieve realtime local intelligence.
content.body: We are building every layer ourselves, from the model through the runtime to the quantization scheme.

content.headline: On-device AI deserves its own frontier lab
content.body: The silicon has shipped. Two billion devices are waiting. The software is the open problem — and it is ours to solve.
